correctness.rationale: Full diagonal idempotents make both corner restrictions Morita equivalences. Transporting the componentwise class gives an intersection, while transporting direct induction gives X⊕Θ(Y); when support tau-tilting its factor class is the join. The cross conditions become the two opposite inclusions, and the semisimple M_2(k^n) family reduces exactly to union versus intersection of subsets.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The fresh source already contains matrix strict-context counterexamples and an intersection obstruction, while classical Morita/torsion theory supplies lattice equivalences. Targeted searches did not locate the general full-corner join-versus-meet theorem, the equality reformulation of the bilateral cross conditions, or the 4^n versus 2^n semisimple family. Older Morita/torsion literature remains a residual terminology risk.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete conceptual description of the strict/full-corner regime complementary to the radical-valued converse: the prescribed class is a meet, direct induction is a join when support tau-tilting, functorial finiteness is exactly intersection functorial finiteness, and an explicit semisimple family shows exponentially many direct-induction successes outside the prescribed-class criterion.
